text: You saw scans versus seeks back in T-SQL Development. This lesson is the DBA version: reading a full graphical execution plan, fast, under pressure, for a query you didn't write and don't yet know what's wrong with.

One button turns this on -- Include Actual Execution Plan, or Ctrl+M. Actual, not estimated, because actual gives you real row counts, and estimated versus actual diverging sharply is itself a common cause of a bad plan.

Plans read right to left. This is a real multi-table join -- Hash Match joins, index scans, compute scalars, each labeled with a cost percentage. The most expensive single operator here is the top Hash Match at eighteen percent.

Three things to check, in order of payoff. Cost percentage shows where the optimizer thinks the time is going. Arrow thickness shows row count. The operator name itself tells you how the data was actually retrieved.
Every other tool in this chapter eventually points you back to a plan like this one to confirm a fix worked. Next up: what Index Seek, Scan, and Lookup specifically mean, operator by operator.
